study.question: Does finite-precision centering and task summation explain the taskwise/aggregate centering gap once auxiliary cotangent collection is held fixed? The observed gap is 0.668362209030126 minus 0.6676314512972833 = 0.0007307577328427 click AUC in g3-r0040-task_direct versus g3-r0040-aggregate_direct, despite exact-arithmetic equivalence.
study.hypothesis: The apparent centering-scope effect is at least partly a numerical optimization artifact: task summation and occupied-row mean subtraction introduce different rounding residuals that can propagate through shared context embeddings. Collecting the same three task cotangents in one backward and performing both sums and centering in FP64 should reduce the scope discrepancy compared with the same collected FP32 graph. This is provisional, not an established explanation, and makes no prediction that FP64 improves click AUC over the incumbent. The centered surrogate backward is a diagnostic; it is not the derivative of its identity forward or a new scalar objective.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit the entire forward model. Earlier task centering used separate autograd nodes, while aggregate centering summed inside the graph first. Here both orders collect three named task cotangents in one node and use the same explicit summation order; reduction precision is a second controlled factor.

Read archived primary DIN section4.3 lines250-283: target-dependent local activation and unnormalized weighted history pooling are inherited through the adapted reference. The proposal changes only training-side cotangent collection, not DIN attention, and claims neither exact original reproduction nor architectural originality.

Read cached primary benchmark section2.3, including INFNet and TokenMixer descriptions. They concern forward information exchange and token mixing. This study retains the local strongest-model family and tests numerical stability of auxiliary backward transfer. Original source-method papers are not fully audited; no priority or superiority claim.

Read pinned upstream shared-table and embedding construction paths. These establish possible shared embedding accumulation routes, not actual active table aliasing or gradient dtype. Product-only auxiliary shared-context transfer from latest controlled sources; residual context blocked; unchanged private task learning and true-label joint loss hook.
Expected inherited parameters: 32192421 total / 31793216 embedding / 399205 dense; must be remeasured by host.
study.proposed_difference: Four standalone modules implement a 2x2 centering-order (task versus aggregate) by auxiliary-reduction-precision (float32 versus float64) factorial. A single custom autograd Function returns three identical context views, bound by label name to cart/fav/buy. Backward promotes each incoming cotangent before any sum, masks empty histories, applies either sum_t C(g_t) or C(sum_t g_t), and casts once at the common collection boundary. Click keeps the original context graph. No added parameter, buffer, RNG, label access in forward, data access, optimizer access, extra backward call or global precision change. This is an integrity diagnostic rather than an efficacy or conflict-resolution claim.
predictions: At common feature map, state and input, every cell has identical initialization, all four train/eval predictions, losses, native Dice updates and private task parameter gradients. Forward masking invariants and task outputs are unchanged.

On host common-state probes with nonzero incoming auxiliary cotangents, the normalized task-versus-aggregate discrepancy after reduction should be lower for FP64 than FP32 when FP32 error is measurable; check absolute/relative errors and occupied-row residual sums before and after the final cast. A rounding hypothesis is not established by AUC alone.

If reduction rounding causes a substantial part of the historical scope gap, the absolute FP64 task-versus-aggregate AUC gap should contract relative to FP32 under this common collection topology. Equal new FP32 cells would instead implicate earlier collection/scheduling effects and make the precision interaction uninformative.

No forward capacity or inference-cost change is predicted. FP64 backward adds small context-array reductions and temporary storage; all four actual training/GPU/wall costs and peak memory must be measured. Neither FP64 nor centering is predicted to exceed incumbent g3-r0034-joint_aligned AUC 0.668473871997858.
falsifiers: Any common-state forward/loss/private-gradient/state difference, wrong task binding, reopened blocked source, current-label access in forward, mask violation or protocol mismatch fails admissibility: stop the affected execution rather than interpreting AUC.

If measurable common-state task/aggregate numerical error does not shrink in FP64, reject the proposed reduction-stage explanation for those probes; inspect incoming cotangent precision and final cast before further training.

If FP64 aligns common-state reductions but comparable training scope differences persist, local reduction precision alone is insufficient; downstream scatter/scheduling, optimizer sensitivity or hidden graph differences remain unresolved.
If FP32 cells already coincide, the earlier task-versus-aggregate gap does not survive common collection; do not attribute a benefit to FP64 or to an auxiliary learning mechanism.

An AUC change without corresponding numerical evidence and repetition is preliminary. No new useful-supervision claim follows if future admissible paired comparisons cannot reproduce advantage over the historical click-only endpoint.
alternative_explanations: Earlier centering-scope gap may arise chiefly from autograd accumulation topology rather than mean-reduction arithmetic; the common collector intentionally changes that topology in every cell.

Shared categorical tables and near-cancelled per-ID gradients can interact with Adagrad, but actual table aliases, per-ID residuals and update sensitivity have not been observed here. Centering across examples does not imply zero per-category gradients.
Mixed-precision upstream task computation, final downcast, primary/auxiliary addition or sparse scatter can dominate even with FP64 reduction.
GPU nondeterminism, single-seed sensitivity, extensive validation selection, batch-coupled Dice state or an implementation defect can explain apparent scope effects.

Earlier beneficial auxiliary supervision, damaging rolled labels, adverse mean-only transfer and failed centered replay are different trajectories. None alone identifies a semantic or interference mechanism.

validation_plan.common_state: At shared state compare four train/eval probabilities, BCEs, native Dice running updates and private module/click-only gradients. In a diagnostic copy give inherited zero output layers the same deterministic nonzero values before numerical probes, so the tested transfer is nontrivial; do not use this diagnostic state for training.
